summary: The root عيش (Eysh) relates to life and sustenance. مَعِيشَةٌ (ma'eeshah) means victuals, living, or the means by which one lives, including food and drink.
lane: مَعِيشَةٌ ذ inf. n. of عَاشَ [q. v.]. (K.) -b2- Also Victuals, living, sustenance, or food and drink by which one lives; (Lth, A, O, K;) as also ; (A;) whence you say that dates are the عَيْش of such a family: (TA:) that whereby life subsists; the means of life or subsistence; (A, K;) as also : (A, TA:) that whereby one lives; as also (A, K, TA) and and ; (TA;) or [the state ] wherein one lives; (A, K, TA;) as also (A) and and : (TA:) the means of obtaining that whereby one lives: (Aboo-Is-hák, TA:) the gain, or earnings, by means of which a man lives; (Mgh, Msb;) as also : (Msb:) the pl. is مَعَايِشُ , (S, O, Msb,) accord. to general opinion, (Msb,) without ء , (S, O, Msb,) when formed from the original of the sing., which is مَعْيِشَةٌ , of the measure مَفْعِلَةٌ ; (S, O;) or because it is from عَاشَ , so that the measure of the pl. is مَفَاعِلُ : (Msb:) but when it is formed from the secondary form of the sing., it is with ء , [ مَعَائِشُ ,] مَفْعِلَةٌ being in this case likened to فَعِيلَةٌ , like as مَصَائِبُ is with ء because the ى [in its sing.] is quiescent; but some of the grammarians hold this latter pl. to be incorrect: (S, O:) all the Basree grammarians hold it to be so: (TA:) or, accord. to some, and مَعِيشَةٌ are from معش ; and the pl. in question is therefore of the measure فَعَائِلُ , with ء . (Msb.) -b3- مَعِيشَةٌ ضَنْكٌ The punishment of the grave: (O, K:) so, accord. to most of the expositors, in the Kur xx. 123: or, as some say, [ strait sustenance ] in the fire of hell. (O, TA.)

headwords.def: (S, A, O, Msb, K,) aor. يَعِيشُ, inf. n. عَيْشٌ (S, O, Msb, K) and مَعَاشٌ and مَعِيشٌ (S, O, K.) and مَعِيشَةٌ and عِيشَةٌ and عَيْشُوشَةٌ (O, K) and in the dial. of El-Azd مَعُوشَةٌ, (K in art. عوش, and TA.) He lived; (S, A, * O, K;) [ he passed life in a particular manner of state:] he became possessed of life. (Msb.) You say,. عَاشَ فُلَانٌ عِيشَةً رَاضِيَةً Such a one lived a pleasant [ life (if we regard عِيشَة as a simple inf.
inf. n. مُعَايَشَةٌ, He lived with him; like as you say عَاشَرَهُ. (TA.)

He (God, S, A) made him to live; (S, A, O, * K;) as also, (O, * K,) inf. n. تَعْيِيشٌ. (TA.) You say, اعاشهُ ٱللّٰهُ عِيشَةً رَاضِيَةٌ [ God made him to live a pleasant life, or state or sort of life ]. (S.)
He constrained himself to obtain the means of life: (S;) or he had what was barely sufficient, of sustenance, nothing remaining over and above it. (TA.)
[ They lived together: one with another ]. You say, تعايشوا بِأُلْفَةٍ وَمَوَدَّةٍ [ They lived together with sociableness and affection, (A, TA.)

[an inf. n. of 1. As a subst.,] Life: (S, O, K;) or particularly animal life. (Kull p. 262.) It is said in a prove., أَنْتَ مَرَّةٌ عَيْشٌ وَمَرَّةٌ جَيْشٌ. meaning, Thou act at one time in an easy state of life, and at one time in the state of life of warriors: (A 'Obeyd, as cited in the TA: [but for عَيْشِ غَزِىّ in my original, we should perhaps read عَيْشٍ عَزِيزٍ, i. e. a difficult state of life: ) or thou benefitest at one time, and injurest at another (TA.
[see 1, in two places. ] A state, (A,) or sort. (TA,) of life. (A, TA.) You say, عَاشَ عِيشَةُ صِدْقٍ, and عِيشَةَ سَوْءٍ, He lived a good sort of life, and an evil sort of life. (TA.)

[ Living: ] having life: and in like manner, but in an intensive sense, (app. meaning having much of the means of life or living well. ): fem. of the former with ة. (Msb.) A man in a good state or condition [ of life ] (Lth, A, O, K.)

and may be used as substantives as well as inf. ns., like مَعَابٌ and مَعِيبٌ; (S, O, TA;) and signify, like مَعِيشَةٌ, That whereby one lives: or that [ place and time ] in which one lives: (TA:) [or rather, they have both these significations; but معاش has generally the latter. whereas معيشة, q.
: see مَعِيشَةٌ, in four places: and مَعَاشٌ.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
